quotes.text: The Stripe fiat-to-crypto onramp lets your customers securely purchase and exchange cryptocurrencies directly from your platform at checkout.
Stripe acts as the *merchant of record*
Use the [Embedded components onramp](https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-components.md) (mobile SDK) to let your customers check out directly in your application.
To access the Stripe onramp, including in [sandboxes](https://docs.stripe.com/sandboxes.md), you must follow these steps to submit your application:
Public preview. For access, [submit an onramp application](https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp.md#submit-your-application).

old_evidence.text: Use the [Embedded components onramp](https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-components.md) (mobile SDK) to let your customers check out directly in your application. [Sign up to join the private preview](https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp.md#sign-up).
We review most onramp applications within 48 hours

findings: The May capture explicitly labeled Stripe-hosted and embedded as public preview, and embedded components mobile SDK as private preview with a separate signup (old lines 21, 36-39). The November same-URL capture still lists all three modes but removes the mobile private-preview signup and collapses the availability row to a single Public preview cell (new lines 22, 37-40). That row does not identify a status separately for embedded or embedded components. The omission cannot establish that mobile access became public preview or generally available, and it cannot by itself prove the old private preview remains current.

The current source's three-row status table (lines 17-21) and related concept's equivalent table (lines 18-20) present May's preview labels without dates. A dated source update should preserve those as historical claims, describe November's ambiguous availability presentation, and avoid asserting account-specific eligibility. The separately indexed embedded-components source still describes private preview, but it is older evidence and not a live eligibility test.

The November overview drops 'or Dapp' from the short description (old lines 6-8; new lines 7-9). That is wording removal, not evidence that decentralized-application integrations are unsupported; the current source and concept should not erase the older Dapp use case solely on this omission.

The onramp application requirement remains explicit even for sandboxes (old lines 12, 25-30; new lines 13, 26-31). Stripe still says it reviews most applications within 48 hours (new line 30), not every application. The current source line 25 should retain the 'most' qualifier.

Stripe's merchant-of-record, fraud/dispute liability, KYC/regulatory handling, saved customer data, and three hosted/web/mobile options remain substantively stable (old lines 10-21, 36-43; new lines 11-22, 37-44). The image URL replacement, list numbering, italic styling and collapsed table formatting are presentation/capture differences.
substantive_changes: Explicit mobile embedded-components private-preview signup and per-mode preview statuses in May are absent from November's overview; November has one ambiguous Public preview availability cell and still requires an application (old lines 21, 38; new lines 22, 39). Treat this as an evidence/status-presentation change, not a verified rollout.
The short overview no longer explicitly mentions Dapps (old lines 6-8; new lines 7-9), without an express support withdrawal.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May's public-preview labels for hosted and embedded and private-preview label for embedded components are dated historical evidence (old lines 21, 38), not established November status.

All three integration modes remain listed: Stripe-hosted redirect, embedded website/mobile webview via Onramp API, and native mobile embedded components via SDK plus APIs (old lines 12-21, 36-41; new lines 13-22, 37-42).
Stripe remains the onramp merchant of record and says it assumes fraud and dispute liability and handles regulatory/KYC/sanctions work (old line 10; new line 11).

Application submission and approval before development, including sandbox access, remain required; Stripe says most applications are reviewed within 48 hours, not all (old lines 25-30; new lines 26-31).
conflicts: Current source lines 19-21 and stripe-crypto-onramp concept lines 18-20 display exact preview statuses without a capture date, while new raw line 39 lacks per-mode status cells. They need historical/date qualification rather than a manufactured current mobile status.
Current source line 25's unqualified 'Applications reviewed within 48 hours' overstates both raw captures' 'most onramp applications within 48 hours' (old line 29; new line 30).

Older standalone embedded-components source still says private preview, whereas this newer overview omits that explicit label; without a same-date capability or account check, no status resolution follows.
unresolved_questions: What November 2026 preview/access status applies separately to embedded web and embedded components mobile is not stated unambiguously in the captured availability row (new line 39).
Whether a specific Stripe account has onramp approval, sandbox access, mobile SDK preview access, or an approved Dapp integration is outside this documentation snapshot.
The absence of Dapp wording does not resolve Dapp support, and the removed private-preview signup does not establish a release date or rollout.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp, the November capture still lists the three onramp modes and requires an application even for sandboxes (new lines 13-31). Compared with May's explicit per-mode public/private preview labels and mobile signup (old lines 21, 38), it shows only one Public preview availability cell and omits the signup (new lines 22, 39). [[source-stripe-crypto-onramp]] needs a dated qualification; the page does not prove mobile public access.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp, [[source-stripe-crypto-onramp]] should preserve May's three-mode and private-mobile-preview evidence as historical (old lines 12-21, 36-41), while reporting the November availability ambiguity and continuing application requirement (new lines 13, 22, 26-31, 37-40). The shorter platform wording at new lines 7-9 does not prove the old Dapp use case at old lines 6-8 was withdrawn. Stripe says most applications are reviewed within 48 hours, not all (old line 29; new line 30).
